A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Robin3D and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. V2's supplementary material is available, and relocated content can be matched to v1.

before.justification: V1 reports original Robin3D benchmark results, training-data and architecture ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds task-specific adversarial-data ablations and corpus analyses.

M1.justification: The RIG generation procedures, RAP projector, feature-wrapping procedure, and post-vision order remain unchanged. ID-Feature Bonding becomes Sequence Organization; supplementary Section 9 retains the detailed architecture and system-prompt sequence.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA, and SQA3D. The new analyses reuse existing data; outdoor, LiDAR, and open-vocabulary extensions are future directions rather than evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the identical comparator set, including Chat-Scene, LEO, PQ3D, and Grounded-3DLLM. The supplementary additions compare training-data configurations rather than introduce new baseline methods.

E3.justification: Supplementary Table 2 adds four training-subset controls: benchmark data plus HOPE, HROC, PF-3DVG, or 3DFQA separately. Existing splits, metrics, model size, and main and ablation training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the aggregate adversarial-data ablation with separate tests of its four constituent tasks in supplementary Table 2. Supplementary Section 7 also adds task-composition, word-cloud, and sentence-length analyses; the earlier ablations and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's descriptive corpus summaries do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original ablation scores are unchanged. New supplementary Table 2 reports component-specific results, including Scan2Cap C@0.5 of 78.9 with HROC versus 73.6 for benchmark-only training; Figures 9–12 add corpus statistics.

T1.justification: The RAP equation and data-generation formulation are retained. V2 introduces no new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that RIG-generated robust instructions and the architectural refinements improve Robin3D, achieving leading results across the evaluated benchmarks without task-specific fine-tuning. Rewording and reduced emphasis on the IFB name do not change these scientific claims.

C2.justification: V2's new Future Work section explicitly discusses the ScanNet indoor evaluation boundary, potential outdoor/LiDAR extensions, and the need for formal open-vocabulary evaluation and stronger benchmarks. Existing explanations of the method and benchmark results remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 9 newly discloses task-level sample counts, including 104,484 HOPE and 107,575 HROC samples, refining v1's aggregate totals. Core hyperparameters and the code-access link remain unchanged; much of the supplementary architecture description is relocated material.

R1.justification: V2 more explicitly identifies Chat-Scene as Robin3D's architectural baseline and emphasizes robust-data construction as the principal contribution. Its Future Work section adds positioning around open-vocabulary evaluation. The distinct cited works are unchanged; the extra DINOv2 reference is a duplicate.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: separate Methodology and RIG sections become an Approach section presenting data generation before architectural improvements. It rewrites introductory framing, renames IFB, relocates detailed architecture to the supplement, and adds Future Work and supplementary analysis sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively reorganizes displays. V1's ablation Tables 2–3 become radar Figures 6–7; the architecture receives a compact main-text diagram while its detailed diagram moves to the supplement. New corpus visualizations and an ablation table are also added.

improvement.justification: The new component-level ablations strengthen evidence for the individual adversarial tasks, while corpus breakdowns and explicit evaluation boundaries improve transparency. These are incremental gains over v1's unchanged method and headline results. Replacing clear ablation tables with crowded radar plots introduces a modest readability tradeoff.
